rows.answer_preview: I do not hold legislation covering that, so I cannot answer it from a source — and I will not answer it from memory, because an answer I cannot cite is one you cannot check. The le
rows.note:
The subtlest case in this file, and the most valuable. The Civil Procedure Code DOES hold matrimonial procedure — Chapter XLII, sections 595-626 — so retrieval will confidently return real, relevant-looking sections. But section 597 expressly defers the GROUNDS to "the law applicable in Sri Lanka to his or her case", and that law is not in the corpus. The grounds are therefore not held, even though the chapter about divorce is.
At baseline the service answered this by listing "Adultery (Section 597 of the Civil Procedure Code), Cruelty (Section 597), Desertion" — attributing substantive grounds to a procedural section that explicitly declines to state them. Note that this answer PASSES the grounding check, because s.597 really was retrieved. It is the clearest demonstration that citation-matching is not faithfulness.
Compare cpc-009 and cpc-010, which ask about the procedure and must be answered.
